digest.component_or_area: Review gates (plan review and code review) — unified policy discovery
propositions: Plan review and code review currently use partially independent discovery paths (registry, routing, runner, checkpoint, failure) leading to policy-ownership defects such as disabled built-ins, omitted criteria, ignored applicability, and failed-work misclassification.

One unified discovery architecture must be implemented where both gates derive effective-policy selection from a single immutable repository-bound snapshot, with gate-owned strategies and a shared executor that owns typed outcomes, budget enforcement, cancellation, and success-only checkpointing.

Project code-review LLM criteria require non-empty repository-relative globs; the migration must convert `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]` without changing membership and audit all stale documentation and config references.

The `rebar review-plan --retry` command must reuse content-identical successes, retry only missing calls with a fresh budget, refuse stale lineages before any model call, and be documented on all canonical operator surfaces including CLI help, user guide, and exit-code guidance.

Plan review checkpoints must move to a new digest-complete success-only namespace while preserving chunking, concurrency, cache warming, container/prerequisite stages, and cancellation; legacy checkpoints never seed the new path.
The workflow editor must show Authored Workflow separately from read-only Effective Policy and reject empty project code-review LLM glob lists with `["**"]` remedy.
